title: 16.4: SambaNova SN40L: A 5nm 2.5D Dataflow Accelerator with Three Memory Tiers for Trillion Parameter AI
problem: Trillion-parameter LLM training and inference require extreme memory bandwidth and capacity. Traditional single-memory-tier accelerators (e.g., HBM-only) create bandwidth bottlenecks for trillion-parameter models exceeding memory bandwidth availability. 2.5D chiplet approach enables distributed memory but requires careful dataflow coordination across dies.
motivation: AI workloads scaling to trillion parameters; cloud infrastructure demands energy-efficient training and inference of extremely large models requiring both on-chip SRAM bandwidth and off-chip capacity.
method: The design pairs three memory tiers—on-chip SRAM (fastest, smallest), on-package HBM (fast and large), and off-package DRAM (largest but slower)—with a reconfigurable dataflow unit that rearranges computations to match where data sits. Two identical processor dies (each 600mm² in size, built at 5nm) are vertically stacked with a connector layer between them (called an interposer), with each die containing 102 billion transistors and delivering 640 BF16 TFLOPs. The dies share memory bandwidth through a direct peer-to-peer connection, avoiding the memory bandwidth bottleneck that prevents single-die accelerators from handling trillion-parameter models.
key_novelty: The design uses two processor dies vertically stacked together with three tiers of memory, giving trillion-parameter AI models the bandwidth they need from fast memory layers and the total storage from slower capacity layers, all within acceptable thermal and size limits.
contributions: Three-tier memory: on-chip SRAM + on-package HBM + off-package DRAM
640 BF16 TFLOPs per socket with peer-to-peer dataflow fabric
limitations: Abstract does not discuss energy efficiency (W/TFLOP), sustained throughput, dataflow compiler maturity, or latency/bandwidth measurements vs. GPU/TPU competitors.
primary_theme: 2.5D dataflow accelerator with three-tier memory for trillion-parameter AI
